States that the plant or part has no chlorophyll (mycoheterotrophs, parasites). The missing thing is a chemical, not a PO part, so the rule needs a ChEBI id, which was not checked in the repository files.
Partly transparent = low opacity, which is PATO translucent (as 'pellucid', rule C237).
PATO reniform has 'bean shaped' as a RELATED synonym; seeds and embryos 'resembling a bean' are kidney-shaped. 'Fruit bean-like' may mean a legume-like pod, so this is not certain.

'Inflorescences thyrses' says the inflorescence is a thyrse; PO has no thyrse class and FLOPO thyrse-like covers the architecture. The 'anthèle' example is a different inflorescence type and should not use this rule.

label: easily detached
definition: A shedability quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's disposition to separate readily from the structure to which it is attached when touched or disturbed.
reason: The ease with which a part breaks off is a diagnostic character (cactus segments, bulbils, perianth bristles). PATO deciduous inheres in the plant that sheds, and caducous means 'falling early', which is a different idea.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (part of the bearer: margin) with red (PATO_0000322)
reason: A colour on a region of the part: the bearer is the margin of the leaf or anther and the quality is red. No new term is needed.
'Scarcely' grades the value 'thickened' (a PATO synonym of increased thickness), as '±' and 'sub-' do; it is not a quality of its own.
Negates PATO auriculate, as 'unlobed' = not lobed (rule C239).
Negates PATO elongated. 'In fruit' in the racemes example is a stage, recorded separately.

label: comal
definition: An aggregated quality inhering in a set of leaves or other shoot organs by virtue of their being crowded into a tuft at the apex of the stem.
reason: A term from the study of mosses (bryology) for leaves or perichaetia crowded at the stem tip. FLOPO rosulate means a radiating cluster on a shortened axis, usually basal, which is not the same.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: cylindrical PATO_0001873 and ovate/ovoid PATO_0001891)
reason: A compound of two 3-D shape values, and both have terms.
Parts (veins, leaves, partitions) set at equal intervals have a repeatable, predictable placement. This is the regular counterpart of FLOPO distant and approximate.

label: hair-tipped
definition: A pointed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ending in a fine hair-like point.
reason: Sibling of FLOPO:0991210 spine-tipped. In mosses the hair-point is a hyaline extension of the leaf, not a trichome, so a 'trichome present' rule would be wrong.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: laciniate FLOPO:0991116 and ciliate margin)
reason: Two values run together: the margin is cut into narrow segments and is ciliate. Each is annotated on its own, so no new term is needed.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: depressed FLOPO:0991103 and ovate/ovoid PATO_0001891)
reason: Ovoid but flattened from above. Unlike 'depressed-globose' (= oblate, rule C170) it has no single term, so the two values combine.
'-escent' here means slightly scabrous, so it is a graded scabrous, like 'sub-' words in the approximate-value pattern.

label: pseudolateral
definition: A positional quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of its being terminal on its axis but appearing lateral because it is overtopped by an erect bract or shoot that continues the line of the stem.
reason: A standard character in Juncaceae, Cyperaceae and others. Lateral or terminal alone would state the opposite of the truth.
A pseudo-umbel is an inflorescence, often a contracted cyme, that resembles an umbel. This is exactly FLOPO umbelliform.

label: scapose
definition: A structural quality inhering in a whole plant by virtue of its flowers being borne on a leafless peduncle (scape) arising from the base of the plant, the plant having no leafy aerial stem.
reason: A 'peduncle present' rule would lose that the stem is leafless and arises from the base, which is the point of the habit. 'Subscapigerous' goes through the approximate-value pattern.
An aril, calyx tube or pistil that is scarcely developed is reduced to a trace, as with 'rudimentary' (rule C142) and 'obsolete' (C234).
Same as rule C341 for 'parallel-veined'.
A count of nodes in a word. 'Several' is not a number (held as measurement_value_not_numeric), and the ending 'noded' still needs a row in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv.

label: stoloniform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's resembling a stolon: long, slender and with long internodes.
reason: It is said of rhizomes, branches and stems that look like stolons without being stolons. It is a sibling of the '-like' shapes such as spike-like.
A biparous (dichasial) cyme produces two branches at each node, as with 'dichotomous' = bifurcated (rule C199). The bearer stays cyme inflorescence (PO_0030126).

reason: A compound of two surface-pattern values, and both have terms.
An outer lip or bract that is 'ray-like' looks like the strap-shaped ligule of a ray floret. It may also imply spreading, which this rule does not capture.
The same word as the existing FLOPO class (French 'ruminé'); it applies to seeds, endosperm and cotyledons.
